Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and changes in accuracy for different metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.84 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.1, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2.  A blue line, marked with circular data points and error bars, represents “Final Accuracy” and begins at approximately 0.82 at an initial confidence of 0.84, fluctuates between approximately 0.88 and 0.96, and ends at approximately 0.91 at an initial confidence of 0.99. An orange line, marked with square data points and error bars, represents “Δ Accuracy” and begins at approximately 0.68 at an initial confidence of 0.84, declines to approximately 0.58 at an initial confidence of 0.88, and ends at approximately 0.64 at an initial confidence of 0.99. A green line, marked with triangular data points and error bars, also represents “Δ Accuracy” and begins at approximately 0.44 at an initial confidence of 0.84, increases to approximately 0.62 at an initial confidence of 0.92, and ends at approximately 0.71 at an initial confidence of 0.99.
